FIELD REFERENCE

Black drum fish in Spanish: names, size and trip tips

The Spanish names for black drum fish are corvina negra and tambor negro. ITIS lists both for Pogonias cromis, and Mexico’s CONABIO uses tambor negro. Look for the whisker-like barbels beneath the chin. Before a coastal trip, match the scientific name to the local rules rather than relying on a translated name alone.

Updated 2026-11-22 · Castward

How do you identify a black drum fish?

Key factDetail
Scientific namePogonias cromis (Texas Parks and Wildlife).
Spanish namesCorvina negra and tambor negro (ITIS); tambor negro is the CONABIO page title.
Other namesDrum and tambour (Louisiana Sea Grant); Texas drum and sea drum (TPWD).
Best identification checkChin barbels. Red drum and sheepshead lack these barbels (FWC).
Small fishLouisiana Sea Grant calls common 1–10 lb fish “puppy drum”.
Large fishTPWD describes many bull drum catches at 30–40 lb. These are not promised catch sizes.
Maximum lengthFWC lists up to 67 inches. This is a species maximum, not a legal size limit.
Trip habitatBays, river mouths, lagoons and bottom structure such as oyster beds, docks and bridge pilings (FWC).

What is black drum fish called in Spanish?

Use corvina negra or tambor negro for Pogonias cromis. ITIS records both Spanish names alongside black drum in English. Mexico’s CONABIO labels the species tambor negro. When you discuss a trip or read a fish list, carry the scientific name with the common name to make the species clear.

Read the source

When should you plan a black drum trip?

Choose the region before the month. Texas Parks and Wildlife describes large drum schools before spawning and February–March catches around deeper bays, channels and jetties. Louisiana Sea Grant gives a January–April spawning window. These are regional life-cycle patterns, not open-season dates or a guarantee that fish will bite.

Read the source

How do black drum change as they grow?

Young black drum have dark bars that disappear as the fish grows. Texas Parks and Wildlife describes lengths of about 6 inches after one year, 12 after two and 16 after three. Colour also varies with the water. Use the chin barbels as well as colour when you identify a fish.

Read the source

What bait and access should a visitor consider?

North Carolina DEQ describes black drum trips from banks, surf and anchored boats. Its bait examples include shrimp, cut fish, clams and pieces of crab. Pick a lawful access point before the drive. Then check local bait rules, the tide and the current forecast for that specific water.

Read the source

What do black drum eat?

Black drum feed along the bottom. Their chin barbels help them find food, and strong teeth in the throat crush shells. North Carolina DEQ lists clams, mussels, oysters and crabs among their foods. This explains why a bottom presentation matters more than a bait that drifts high above the fish.

Read the source

What should you know about black drum?

Are black drum and red drum the same fish?

No. They are related fish. Black drum have chin barbels; red drum lack them. Compare both species before you apply a size limit.

How can I tell a young black drum from a sheepshead?

Both can have dark bars. Check under the chin: FWC identifies barbels on black drum, but not on sheepshead.

How big is a puppy drum?

Louisiana Sea Grant uses “puppy drum” for commonly caught black drum of 1–10 lb. The nickname is not a legal size category.

Is black drum good to eat?

Louisiana Sea Grant rates smaller black drum more highly for food and describes larger fish as coarser. Check local consumption advice and harvest rules before keeping a fish.

What is the legal size for black drum?

The rule depends on the state and water. Use the official fisheries links below for your destination; a species maximum is not a keeper limit.

Do I need a licence for a black drum trip?

Check the licence rules for your chosen state, access point and trip type. A bank trip and a charter can have different licence requirements.
